fields.meta_description: Build a maintenance request form that asks about entry and pets, alerts one person on emergencies, and logs repairs by unit. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Maintenance Request Form That Routes Every Repair
fields.hero_description: Build a maintenance request form that asks where the problem is and whether to enter, then sends it to the right technician.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Asks and Where It Goes
fields.features_subheading: A maintenance request form does its job when the technician arrives knowing which fixture failed and how to get in.
fields.feature_1:
Where the problem is and who may go in

The form asks which room and which fixture, whether a technician may enter when nobody is home, and whether a pet is inside. Each answer saves as its own field on the request.
fields.feature_2:
Each trade goes to its own technician

A leak goes to the plumber and a dead outlet to the electrician, or to the vendor who handles that trade. A request left unclaimed for 2 hours escalates to the property manager.
fields.feature_3:
Emergencies skip the line

You choose the answers that count as an emergency, such as water coming through a ceiling or a gas smell. Those requests alert the person on call by email and in the app at once.
fields.feature_4:
Status emails without a phone call

When a visit is booked, the tenant gets an email with the date and time window. A second email follows when the technician marks the job done, with a note on what was fixed.
fields.feature_5:
Every repair on file by unit

The dashboard groups requests by building and unit, and a third leak under the same sink in 60 days shows up on one row. Filter by trade or vendor to see which jobs are still open.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, in your GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the form, with its dashboard and routing rules, as code to your GitHub repository. A developer can then change any part of it outside Emergent.
fields.why_title: Why Run Maintenance Requests on Emergent?
fields.why_description: Every request is a row in a database you own, with no cap on responses, and each row stays tied to its building and unit.

fields.tab_content_1:
Tenants say yes or no to entry up front

Harlow Court's form starts with the unit and the exact fixture. Yusra Pellegrino in unit 4B reports a leak under the kitchen sink, says the plumber may enter while she is out, and notes a dog at home. The work order reaches Dunmore Plumbing with that entry note, and her request saves to Harlow Court's database.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every drawer and outlet lands with its shop

Move-in week at Westmere College brought 38 requests from Alder Hall, sorted by the trade each resident picked: 22 furniture, 9 plumbing, and 7 electrical. Ezra Narvaez's desk drawer in room 214 came off its track, and his request posted to the carpentry shop's Slack channel. A dead outlet went to the electricians.
fields.tab_content_3:
Slow drain in 1108, reported from the hallway

Housekeepers at the Ashgrove Hotel file requests from their phones between rooms. Paloma Grieve reports that the shower in room 1108 drains slowly and adds a photo. Anselm Haddow, the engineer on shift, gets the request on a card addressed to him in the app, with the room number and her photo.
fields.tab_content_4:
Owner signs off when estimates pass $500

Brightfern Rentals sends any repair estimated at $500 or less straight to its vendor. Of today's 4 requests, 3 went out that way. The water heater at 233 Halsey St came back at $1,240, and owner Henrietta Vosburgh got an email asking her to approve it. The job waits for her answer before anyone is booked.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Maintenance Request Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a maintenance request form that sends each repair, with entry details, to the right technician.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Walk one unit and list what breaks
fields.howto_step_1_des: Go through one unit and note everything in it that can fail. Next to each item, write what a technician needs to know before the visit, such as the model number or where the shutoff valve is. That list becomes your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the form in plain English: the questions each tenant answers and who handles each kind of repair. Emergent turns that prompt into the form, its routing rules, and the database behind them. A follow-up prompt changes any part of it later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Assign every trade to a person or a vendor, such as plumbing to the plumber you call first and locks to your locksmith. Add a fallback, such as the property manager, for any request that fits no trade or waits too long without an owner.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the answers that cannot wait until morning, such as a burst pipe, a gas smell, or a lockout, and name who is on call each night. Keep the list short. An alert should still mean that someone gets up and goes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a dollar limit for approvals
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the estimate above which an owner or a manager approves a repair before anyone is booked. Requests at or under that amount go straight to the vendor, and anything above it waits for a reply to the approval email. Put the limit in your prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test with three requests of your own
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit three requests yourself: a routine repair, an emergency, and one over your dollar limit. Check that each reaches the right person, that the alert gets to whoever is on call, and that the tenant's confirmation email shows the right unit.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on the free tier, which covers building and publishing, or put the form on a custom domain, which uses credits. Add the link to the lease packet and to a sign by the mailboxes, where tenants will see it the next time a faucet drips.

faq_plan.q: What is a maintenance request form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a maintenance request form?

prov.original: What is a maintenance request form?

faq_plan.a: A maintenance request form is what a tenant, guest, or employee fills in to report something that needs repair. It records what is broken, where it is, and how to reach the person who reported it. Those answers give whoever handles repairs enough to schedule the work.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a maintenance request form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder: what tenants should answer and where each kind of repair should go. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. To start from fields tenants already know, paste the questions from your old paper maintenance request form template into the prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should a maintenance request form include?
faq_plan.a: Include the requester's name and phone number, the unit, the room and fixture, a description of the problem, and the times someone can get in. Add a question on entering while nobody is home, a pets field, and an optional photo. A housing maintenance request form for a residence hall swaps the unit for the hall and room number.

faq_plan.q: Is a maintenance request form the same as a work order?
faq_plan.a: No. In UpKeep's definition, a work request is submitted by staff or customers to request that work be performed on an asset. A work order is an authorization from the maintenance planner to perform maintenance tasks, and it is created once a request is approved. For help beyond repairs, such as IT, a service request form fits better.

faq_plan.q: Should a maintenance request form ask for permission to enter?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask it as a yes or no question, then add a short field for entry notes, such as a lockbox code or a cat that must stay in the bedroom. The answer tells the technician whether to book a time with the tenant or go in while the unit is empty. Give the notice your lease promises before anyone enters.

faq_plan.q: What counts as an emergency on a maintenance request form?
faq_plan.a: You decide. Put anything on the list that can damage the building or put someone at risk before morning. Good candidates are flooding, a sparking outlet, no heat in freezing weather, and an entry door that will not lock. Show those as checkboxes on the form, and have a checked box reach whoever is on call that night.

faq_plan.q: Can a maintenance request form fill in tenant details automatically?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when tenant records live in the same app. The form asks for the unit and fills in the tenant's name and phone number from the record kept after the tenant screening form was approved. On Emergent, those tenant records and every request sit in one database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a maintenance request form let tenants attach photos?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and keep the upload optional. A picture of a stained ceiling or a washer's error code lets the technician bring the right part on the first visit. For appliances, ask for a second shot of the sticker inside the door that carries the model number, and for cracks, a hand in the frame for scale.

faq_plan.q: What should a hotel maintenance request form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the room or area, the issue, who found it, and whether the room can still be sold tonight. Keep it short enough for housekeepers to fill in on a phone between rooms, with a photo upload and a field for the guest's name when a guest reported it. Emergent forms have no response caps, which matters on a checkout morning with 40 rooms turning over.

faq_plan.q: Should the lease say where to find the maintenance request form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the form's link in the lease with the emergency phone number next to it. Tenants then know where to report a leak before it spreads. If the rental agreement form and the request form live in one app, each signed lease can carry a link to the request form for that unit.

plan.angle: The top 10 for maintenance request form is one institution's portal (a university facilities office, a county, a campus housing office) or a blank template (TemplateLab, Wufoo, Jotform, a CMMS blog's work order template). Each stops at the fields. This page shows the form a landlord, housing office or hotel runs, built around what gets a repair done on the first trip: where in the unit the problem is, whether the technician may enter, pets and entry notes, a photo, emergencies that alert one person, the trade that decides who goes, the owner's approval above a dollar limit, and every request kept by unit in a database the business owns. Four tabs are four real places requests come from (an apartment building, a college residence hall, a hotel, a portfolio of single-family rentals); the FAQ answers the definition, the request versus work order question and the build choices a property manager makes.
